segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics news digest for August 31st, 2026.
Today we cover new findings on humanoid robot behavior, advancements in sensor technology, and exciting developments in AI applications.
From Robohub, "When expressive humanoid robots are awkward, people become wary – new brain study".
This report details a study investigating the relationship between expressive humanoid robots and human trust based on conversational performance.

Fifty participants interacted with the expressive robot Pepper, and errors in conversation led to increased oxytocin levels, which correlated with decreased trust and reduced reliance on the robot's advice.
This effect was linked to brain activity observed in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and the medial prefrontal cortex, illustrating the brain's processing of social awkwardness.
Animated robot errors were interpreted as social violations rather than simple technical faults, directly impacting the level of trust established with the technology.
This research indicates that the expressiveness of robots directly influences human perception of mistakes and subsequently shapes trust in artificial intelligence systems.
And that's all for your daily dose of robotics.
Remember, even our silicon friends need a little software update sometimes.
Have a wonderfully wired evening, and we'll see you tomorrow!
